To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the self-interacting, quasilinear force that governs the particle motion is completely specified by the equilibrium conditions, that the force can give rise to a nonvanishing, effective viscous fluid pressure, and that the effective pressure is related to the self-interacting force by an equation that can be solved for the latter in terms of the former.

(i) The equilibrium states of a self-interacting gas are determined by the equilibrium conditions and the form of the self-interacting force, and (ii) The effective viscous pressures on the fluid phenomeno- logical level are given by the equilibrium states of the gas.
the effective pressure of an equilibrium gas can be negative and that this pressure is proportional to the square of the temperature, which can be negative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics.
the kinetic theory of a classical relativisitic gas of particles which move in a self-interacting force field.
a kinetic theory for nongeodesic particle motion, which may be useful in the context of cosmological models of the universe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of a relativistic gas, the effective viscous fluid pressure is the result of a nontrivial interplay of self-interacting forces, particle collisions and the geometry of spacetime.
the self-interacting force is the most important ingredient of a kinetic theory of relativistic gases, which is capable of describing the evolution and structure of the early universe.
the effective viscous pressure of a self-interacting, relativistic gas is the only possible source of a cosmological acceleration of the expansion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the self-interaction of a classical, relativistic gas is a powerful tool in the search for a unified description of the early universe.
, in the absence of any external forces, self-interacting gas particles may move in a way which is consistent with the laws of classical mechanics, but which may be far away from the geodesics.
the effective pressure tensor is a tensorial function of the fluid 4-velocity and the fluid 4-moment tensor, and that it is determined in terms of the equilibrium conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cosmological particle creation rate is a direct measure of the effective viscous pressure.
the effective viscous pressures are in general not of the Navier-Stokes type, and that the particle interactions are responsible for the deviation from the Navier-Strokes form.
the effective pressure tensor in the fluid description of the gas may have a nontrivial dependence on the fluid's velocity.
